title: RNAD: A Regime-Normalized, Tail-Robust and Direction-Aware Loss for Deep Time-Series Forecasting
content: Financial time-series forecasting is commonly optimized with mean squared error (MSE), yet volatility clustering, heavy tails, and regime shifts make a fixed quadratic objective poorly suited. Existing robust losses improve resistance to extreme errors but lack adaptive volatility normalization and explicit directional supervision, while directional objectives such as Generalized Mean Absolute Directional Loss (GMADL) do not integrate volatility scaling, tail adaptation, and noise-aware directional weighting. We introduce Regime-Normalized Adaptive Directional Loss (RNAD), a model-agnostic training objective combining online volatility normalization via batch-scale estimates and an exponential moving average, tail-gated interpolation between quadratic and Charbonnier penalties, and noise-gated directional supervision that attenuates near-zero returns. RNAD requires no architectural changes, adds only a scalar state buffer, and incurs no inference-time overhead. Across nine financial assets, four architectures (PatchTST, iTransformer, N-HiTS, TimeXer), five losses, and three seeds under chronological splits, RNAD achieves the lowest mean RMSE for every backbone, reducing RMSE by 0.086–0.882 units versus the strongest non-RNAD baseline. It also improves MAE and directional accuracy (DA), with the lowest RMSE on all nine assets when paired with PatchTST. Four-step forecasts on US500 and USDJPY improve average DA by 2.39 and 1.41 percentage points, respectively, and reduce flattened RMSE on US500 by 0.3%. Ablations identify directional supervision as the main contributor, with tail adaptation and noise gating providing complementary, regime-dependent gains. Overall, adaptive, volatility-aware loss design offers a lightweight route to better numerical accuracy and directional consistency across financial forecasting architectures.
